title: Influence of Mechanical Loading at Low-Temperature on the Functional Fatigue of Shape Memory Alloys
content: Shape memory alloys (SMAs) are remarkable materials recognized for their superelasticity (SE) and shape memory effect (SME). Their exceptional properties, including significant strain recovery and high energy dissipation capacity, make them ideal for various applications in the automotive, military, aerospace, biomedical, robotics, and MEMS industries [1-3]. However, these alloys can experience functional fatigue, which refers to the deterioration of key functional properties, such as recoverable strain, hysteresis loop width, dissipated energy, critical transformation stress, transformation temperatures, phase transformation capacity, and associated critical stresses [4,5]. Functional degradation arises from strain incompatibility between the austenite and martensite phases, resulting in localized stress concentrations and the formation of dislocations at their interfaces, specifically along the habit planes [6].
